title: COLOSSAL ESCALATION // EMBODIED SCALE
intent: Push the existing body-relative scale system beyond room-scale changes into monumental and world-scale presence, while preserving identity and continuity.
law: At every tier, the subject remains recognizably themself; the world must change its relationship to them.

tiers.name: OVERSIZED BASELINE
signals: clothing under visible tension
furniture becomes undersized
doorways frame the body tightly
other people adjust their spacing
tiers.world_change: Personal rooms begin to feel designed for a former body.

tiers.name: ROOM-DOMINANT
tiers.scale: the body becomes the room's primary spatial reference
signals: movement requires deliberate turning
the subject occupies major portions of the frame
floor and structure answer movement
ordinary routes become constrained
tiers.world_change: Rooms are reorganized around circulation, clearance, and rest.

tiers.name: BUILDING-SCALE PRESENCE
tiers.scale: architecture is experienced in relation to the subject
signals: doorways and corridors read as thresholds
windows and balconies become scale markers
the camera must retreat to preserve the whole figure
the building's exterior becomes a measuring surface
tiers.world_change: The building becomes a fitted environment rather than a neutral container.

tiers.name: MONUMENTAL BASELINE
tiers.scale: the subject becomes a landmark within the surrounding district
signals: streets and plazas establish distance
nearby structures provide comparative scale
shadow and silhouette dominate the scene
movement changes how the surrounding area is navigated
tiers.world_change: Maps and public spaces are redrawn around the subject's presence.

tiers.name: LANDSCAPE-SCALE
tiers.scale: the subject is legible across a broad landscape
signals: terrain supplies the measuring grid
weather and light provide scale cues
the camera shifts to aerial or distant viewpoints
landmarks become body-relative reference points
tiers.world_change: The landscape becomes a relational anatomy of ridges, routes, and boundaries.

tiers.name: MYTHIC COLOSSUS
tiers.scale: the subject functions as a living geographic or mythic feature
signals: settlements orient themselves around the figure
routes and ceremonies encode their presence
the world records recurring changes in light, sound, and movement
the subject's identity is carried through symbols and remembered encounters
tiers.world_change: The subject becomes part of the world's geography without losing personhood.

escalation_protocol: Establish a recognizable baseline and one stable witness.
Increase a selected dimension: width, height, depth, reach, or total mass.
Propagate the change into at least three affordances or spatial relations.
Show a sensory/environmental response, not just a numerical claim.
Preserve one familiar feature, gesture, object, or relationship as a continuity anchor.
Record the new baseline and leave the altered world state in memory.

composition_rules.body_first: The subject remains the focal presence; scale devices support rather than replace the body.
composition_rules.extreme_girth: Communicate width and depth through silhouette, side clearance, turning radius, contact with clothing, and the amount of space displaced.
avoid: generic size adjectives without visible evidence
erasing facial identity or signature features

scene_seeds: The same doorway, revisited after several growth events, now frames only a fraction of the subject.
A familiar companion stands beside the subject while the camera retreats from room view to district view.
The building's old entrance remains intact as a preserved record of the earlier baseline.
At monumental scale, a plaza becomes a measuring instrument through paving, columns, and human silhouettes.
At landscape scale, the subject's shadow crosses a route that once took minutes to walk.
The subject returns to a remembered place; the place has adapted, but a small original detail remains untouched.
